♡Family Today♡

Another perfect one — sunny, 68, dead calm this morning at 46 degrees. The barometer set a new record again overnight. The Harvest Moon is Saturday, full at 12:48 in the afternoon, so Saturday evening at moonrise is when to look. Clear sky forecast for it.
  • Sep 26Harvest Moon, full at 12:48 p.m.
  • Sep 27Chargers at Buffalo, Jets at Detroit — both 1:00
  • Nov 3Election Day
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

Outdoor window Wide open again, and it holds all the way to Wednesday, which touches 74. Seven days without a drop of rain in the forecast. Saturday at 71 is the pick for anything that needs doing outside. Pollen Ragweed high.
The nor'easter: Long Island's weekend, hour by hour. The storm is strengthening off the coast this morning and turning north. About eighteen million people from Maine to Florida are under coastal alerts.

Today — partly sunny and windy on Long Island, upper sixties, northeast gusts 30 to 35 and 39 on the east end, higher offshore. Coastal flooding at high tide. Friday — cloudy, windy, showers arriving, minor to moderate flooding on the high tides; this is when it turns. Saturday and Sunday are the worst of it — periods of moderate rain, gusts over 40 and possibly 50, mainly in Suffolk County, with scattered power outages considered likely. Under an inch of rain in most scenarios; the wind and the water are the problem, not the rain. It tapers Sunday night.

Saturday's full moon puts astronomical high tides underneath all of it, which is why the flooding forecast is worse than the rain forecast. The track is still the variable: a shift west means heavier rain and stronger wind for Nassau and Suffolk; a shift east means wind and beach damage without the soaking. Nobody east of Albany should plan anything outdoors Saturday.

🍂The Turning🍂

Still at the starting line out here. The spotters have Niagara, Chautauqua and Monroe counties at essentially no change, with a trace of color logged near Niagara Falls and five percent down in Geneseo. The pattern this week — sun all day, mid-forties at night — is what moves those numbers, so next Wednesday's report should look different.
The Adirondacks are at thirty-five percent already. Color starts in the mountains and walks south and west; the Southern Tier goes before the lake plain does, because the lakes hold heat into October and keep the trees green a week or two longer than the hills.

☾The Almanac Sky☾

Waxing gibbous, 95 percent, in Pisces, rising at 6:11 this evening — near enough to full that it will look full. The Harvest Moon proper is Saturday, and the reason it has a name is that it rises close to sunset several nights running, which once gave farmers extra light to finish a harvest.
Sun 7:04a – 7:09p · 12h 5m · 3h 19m shorter than June 21
Next new moon Sat, Oct 10 · Harvest Moon Sat, Sep 26
Tonight Saturn rises in the east at 7:37. Jupiter comes up at 3:18 a.m. Two days past the equinox, and the nights are now the longer half of the day until March.
Aries
Saturn sits at eleven degrees of your sign, nearly still — it has barely moved in a week, which is what a planet does before it turns direction. Slow is not stuck. Things that feel stalled right now are waiting on something outside your control. Kaylani, Luka
Cancer
Mars is at twenty-seven and a half degrees of Cancer, two and a half from the door. Its last full day in your sign is close. Use it. Gregg
Leo
Jupiter at eighteen degrees of Leo and Mercury still sextile from Libra, now separating. The easy stretch of the past week is ending, which means the thing you meant to say should get said today rather than next week. Leah, Tommy
Virgo
The Sun is at one degree of Libra, two days out of your sign. The traditional read is that the two weeks after your season ends are the ones where you finally notice what you actually finished. Worth doing honestly. Derek, Joanne
Scorpio
The Moon in Pisces trines Venus in your sign today — water to water, the easiest aspect Venus has made in a week. The Venus-Pluto square is finally separating. Whatever it stirred up is on its way out. Ariel, Claire, Garret
Positions computed for noon today at 14120. The sky is real; the readings are for fun.

☰The Barograph · 14120☰

Low · 13/100
30.50″
↑ a record again
30.50, and still rising Another record, six hundredths above yesterday. Thirty and a half inches is genuinely unusual for September in this part of the country. Three days of slow climbing is about the gentlest thing a barometer can do to a migraine sufferer, and the risk number is the lowest it has been since the log started. The same dome is what is shoving the nor'easter against the coast.

✶The Ledger✶

People under coastal alerts, Maine to Florida
18 million
That is the size of the nor'easter's reach this morning — flooding, rip current and high surf alerts down the entire Eastern Seaboard, while Western New York sits under the clearest sky of the year. Same weather map.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Nor'easter Strengthens Off the Coast

Eighteen million people from Maine to Florida are under coastal alerts. Hatteras Island faces four feet of water and significant overwash; the peak for the Northeast is Friday to Sunday.

2

Trump Addresses the General Assembly

He used the U.N. rostrum to attack the institution itself. Several delegations walked out.

3

Hormuz Framework Said to Be Signed

Iran and Oman have reportedly reached terms on traffic through the strait. Oil fell on the news; diesel is still above six dollars.

4

Measles Outbreak Widens in Pennsylvania

State health officials confirmed additional cases this week. Vaccination rates in the affected county sit below the level that stops transmission.

☑ The Ballot · 40 days to Election Day · early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

Chautauqua County · Turkeys on the Move

Not news, exactly, but the flocks are grouping up and crossing yards in daylight, which is what they do in the last week of September. Watch for them on back roads at dawn and dusk; they do not yield.

2

Monroe County · Harvest Festival Saturday

Northampton Park, the same afternoon the Harvest Moon comes full at 12:48. Weather for it: mostly sunny and 71.

★The Marquee★

1

Sheeran at Gillette Tomorrow

The Loop Tour reaches the stadium whose owner asked for Macklemore's removal, two nights, Friday and Saturday, with no openers and no backing band.

2

The Kennedy Center Fight Moves to Court

Donors and artists are suing over the board's vote to close the building. No closing date has been set.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Three Days to Sunday
Bills · the Chargers at Orchard Park, Sunday at one. Buffalo is 2–0 and rested; Los Angeles is 0–2 and arrives off a loss to the Raiders. Sunny and 69 in the forecast for kickoff, which in late September at Orchard Park is about as good as it gets.
Jets · at Detroit, Sunday at one, indoors and therefore no weather excuses. New York is 1–1 with the best penalty problem in football — thirteen for 156 yards against Green Bay — and the cleanest quarterback play it has had in years.

⚑The Chase⚑

Two Days to Kansas
The Hollywood Casino 400 is Sunday at three on USA, race four of ten. Larson leads Hamlin by a single point. Qualifying is Saturday afternoon. Kansas is a mile-and-a-half with enough grooves to make passing real, which is not true of every track on this schedule.

☾On This Day☾

September 24, 1869 — Black Friday. Two speculators tried to corner the American gold market; the Treasury dumped four million dollars of gold onto it and the price collapsed inside fifteen minutes. Ruin was general.

✧Question of the Day✧

Benjamin Franklin wanted me for the national bird. I travel in a crowd, I can run thirty miles an hour, and I do not get out of the road for anyone. What am I? Answer below the fold.
Question of the Day: The wild turkey. See Plate I, and count them.
